LESSON: COMPOUND PROPORTIONS AND RATES OF WORK

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers 1.2 Cubes and Cube Roots (5 Lessons) • Cubes of numbers by multiplicatio
Topic 1.4: Compound Proportions and Rates of Work
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Compound Proportions and Rates of Work, part of Numbers 1.2 Cubes and Cube Roots (5 Lessons) • Cubes of numbers by multiplicatio in Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: What are proportions? 2. Why do we work fast?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss and divide quantities into proportional parts and express them as a fraction,

2. compare and write different ratios,

3. determine compound proportions using ratios,

4. work out rates of work,

5. play games on rates of work using IT devices. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss and divide quantities into proportional parts and express them as a fraction,
2. compare and write different ratios,
3. determine compound proportions using ratios,
4. work out rates of work,
5. play games on rates of work using IT devices. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Compound Proportions and Rates of Work together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship - active community life skills: as learner works with peers to discuss and divide quantities into proportional

parts and express as a fraction.

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving - interpretation and inference: learner works out rates of work.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner commits to working out answers to given tasks on rates.

• Respect: learner works out rates of work cooperatively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-esteem: as learner devices personal strategies to estimate products in multiplication.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Agriculture helps learner estimate harvests, seeds or fertilizer during sowing or application as part of rates of work.
